_doc: Reference briefs for xlite RUINED-CITY terrain/object art (docs/art/REFERENCE_RESEARCH_STEP.md Step 0). Separate file from art_reference_briefs.json because that file's schema is unit-specific (BRIEFS['units'], corpse/downed families) - this one is generic object/tile pieces consumed by gen_terrain_from_brief.py. Every prompt is built from THIS file; never hand-write one that bypasses it. Canon: reference-xlite-art-direction memory - post-apocalyptic wasteland with damaged/worn advanced tech, NOT clean sci-fi. Research grounding (no live web access this session - composed from established genre visual conventions: Fallout ruined townscapes, Mad Max scavenged structures, XCOM 2's ruined ADVENT cities, The Last of Us overgrown/collapsed urban blocks, Metro station/tunnel wear patterns) - every entry's key_features/negatives are written from those conventions, not generic guesses.
style: pixel art, painterly wasteland style, muted rust-red/ash-gray/steel-blue palette with warning-amber accents, high contrast, bold clean readable silhouette, hard top-left directional lighting, weathered worn damaged surfaces, long-abandoned
framing_object: single object, isometric three-quarter view facing front-right, upright standing on the ground, centered, flat solid neutral gray background, no cast shadow, no floor, no scenery
framing_tile: seamless top-down flat texture, fills the entire frame, no object, no character
base_negatives: blurry, jpeg artifacts, text, watermark, signature, cropped, multiple objects, low contrast, washed out, purple tint, monochrome, photo, 3d render, clean pristine new, sci-fi neon, cartoon, sepia
object_negatives: cast shadow, drop shadow, ground shadow, floor, ground plane, base platform, background scenery, character, person, creature, vehicle interior
tile_negatives: object, character, vignette, border, frame, single item
_consistency_note: EVERY key below shares the same style/framing/negatives strings above - that IS the consistency mechanism (user 2026-09-10: 'keep all the artwork to a consistent theme, color scheme, ratio, angle, proportion... keep this consistent always'). gen_terrain_from_brief.py refuses to build a prompt that doesn't route through these shared strings. Raw renders are 1024x1024 same as every other xlite asset; pixelize3.py's existing floodkey+autocrop (objects) / full-frame (tiles, filename must contain 'tile') handles final sizing to the same 64/48/32 grids as everything else in the game - no separate size pipeline.
